status: Experimental sensitivity study - not for construction
boundsMeaning: Low, reference and high are chosen sensitivity cases, not measured site bounds, probabilities or guaranteed worst cases. Conditions outside these cases remain possible.
correction: 8.59 m is the east-west bounding width of a fragmented floor mesh, NOT a verified clear joist span. No central spine beam is proposed. Direction is assessed by local bay and supports below.
basis: First-generation BS EN Eurocodes with the corresponding UK National Annexes as the trial basis. Do not mix generations. Confirm applicable editions at engineering appointment. England Approved Documents are guidance, not a substitute for calculations.
floorLoadBasis: Gk includes an assumed 0.35 kN/m2 lightweight-partition allowance; remaining floor/deck/finish/ceiling/services allowance is 0.40 / 0.65 / 1.00 kN/m2. These are budgets, not measured build-ups. Stone, screed, masonry partitions, baths and heavy storage can exceed them. Qk=1.5 kN/m2 domestic floor area loading; supplier table also includes a separate 2 kN concentrated imposed-load check.

steelStudies.name: West garage door head
steelStudies.basis: Garage joists in the north-south candidate run parallel to this opening, so no distributed floor tributary width is assigned here. Assumed wall/roof-equivalent permanent line load 4 / 7 / 10 kN/m is a sensitivity only. Higher case adds a 10 kN permanent midspan point load. The actual roof, upper facade and edge-floor reactions remain unknown.

steelStudies.name: Gym west full-span steel alternative (not preferred)
steelStudies.basis: Comparison only if the timber stud-wall route cannot be made to work. One gym floor bay only: 4.49 / 2 = 2.245 m tributary width. Assumes simple end supports; neither is established. No gallery, loft or roof reaction included. Higher case adds 10 kN permanent midspan load. Not the preferred scheme.

joistConditions: James Jones Table 16, domestic intermediate floors, service class 1, simply supported, adequately restrained with 22 mm chipboard and 15 mm plasterboard; engineering span, not cut length. Uses 1.35 kN/m2 table conservatively for reference Gk=1.0, without interpolation. Published vibration assumptions include a 4 m floor width; actual room widths and finishes require supplier design. Bearings, holes, hangers, trimming, fire and acoustics remain unverified.
steelConditions: Six-section British Steel S355 UB shortlist. Simple span, major-axis bending, symmetric UDL plus central permanent point load, no axial load/torsion, no holes and effective lateral/torsional restraint assumed. Elastic bending and web shear screen only, not a member approval. Connections, lateral-torsional buckling, patch loading, bearings, robustness, fire and support capacities are not checked. The stated section may be inadequate once these are considered.
steelDeflection: Chosen trial criteria: total characteristic deflection <= min(L/360,10 mm), imposed-only <= L/360. This is a project screening criterion, not a universal regulatory limit. Glazing/masonry may need tighter limits, camber and differential-movement checks.
basementBasis: 3.05 m retained-height illustration from ground datum to underside of current 250 mm base. Effective-stress earth pressure with assumed K0 plus hydrostatic water and uniform surface surcharge. Cantilever base moment is a comparison model, not the designed restraint condition. No beneficial drainage assumed. Adjacent foundations, compaction, heave, swelling, accidental surcharge and flooding above grade are outside these scenarios.
unresolved: No whole-building vertical/lateral load analysis; wind, snow, roof, terrace, storage, plant and vehicle cases remain to be established.
Joist direction is not inferred from a floor bounding box. Measured supports and every opening/void need reconciliation, especially around the galleries.
No ground capacity, settlement, foundation or basement reinforcement design; no safe excavation or temporary-works sequence.
No construction-approved member sizes, lintel schedule, bearing/padstone design or fabrication dimensions.
350+ mm cavity wall build-up differs from the current 230 mm shell; thermal, fire, moisture, acoustic and dimensional coordination remain required.
Engineer and supplier validation is needed BEFORE excavation, demolition, fabrication or construction, followed by site verification.

timberWall.name: Gym glazed load-bearing timber stud wall
timberWall.loadBasis: Upper sensitivity geometry: half 4.49 m gym bay plus half 5.53 m gallery bay = 5.01 m tributary width. Assumes one domestic floor, including the scenario partition budget. Gallery voids may reduce load but are not deducted. Roof/loft/upper masonry and concentrated reactions are NOT automatically included. Headers share load equally between two side-by-side plies, requiring designed connections and bearing to both.
timberWall.basis: Test ordinary graded structural timber first, then UK-supplied LVL if needed. Timber headers and jack/king studs are part of the wall framing, not exposed masonry piers. Stud sizes/spacing and connections remain unselected pending axial/buckling, local bearing and whole-wall checks.
timberWall.coordination: Current heads start at 2.40 m (windows) and 2.333 m (door), with floor underside at 2.60 m: only 200 / 267 / 200 mm head zones. A header, top plates and bearing arrangement must fit together; any required lowering of glazing or floor-depth change must be shown. Adjacent 200 mm solid strips may need minor widening for stud packs. Preserve doorway clear width; revise glazing only as needed.
timberWall.supportBelow: The model has a full basement under this wall. The ground-floor slab is an architectural envelope, not an established support for the stud wall. A designed transfer/rib/wall/beam and foundation load path is needed below; changing to timber does not remove this requirement.

quantityRates.basis: Modular arithmetic for one leaf, per 100 m2 NET wall face. Not a whole-house order. Returns, openings, bond, specials and pack rounding excluded. Block strength/mortar/ties not designed.

formulas.steel: ULS = 1.35G + 1.5Q (one adverse variable action). M=wL²/8+PL/4; R=wL/2+P/2; delta=5wL⁴/(384EI)+PL³/(48EI). E=210000 N/mm². Supplier I cm4 x10000; Wel cm3 x1000. Self weight included per candidate.
formulas.timber: Trial two-ply C24: b=90 mm, h=145/195/220 mm, fm,k=24, fv,k=4, fc90,k=2.5 N/mm², Emean=11000, Gmean=690 N/mm². gammaM=1.3; kmod=.6 permanent and .8 medium-term, both checked; kh=ksys=1, kcr=.67, full end shear. SC1 kdef=.6, domestic psi2=.3. Bending plus shear deformation; final=deltaG(1+.6)+deltaQ(1+.3x.6). Direct bearing indication uses kc90=1 and no effective-length enhancement. Inst <= min(L/300,8mm), final <= min(L/250,10mm) are chosen screening limits. Equal load/bearing to both restrained plies assumed; connections, studs, stability and whole-wall design outstanding.
formulas.joists: Supplier table lookup at engineering span = model face-to-face bay + assumed bearing-centre/tolerance allowance (100/150/250 mm). Not a cut length or designed bearing. Floor loads and actual room width must be validated.
formulas.retaining: p(z)=K0[q+gamma_dry min(z,zw)+(gamma_sat-9.81)max(z-zw,0)]+9.81max(z-zw,0). Integrate p for force and p(H-z) for cantilever base moment. No geotechnical design factors or resistance check.
formulas.uplift: Unfactored uplift=9.81 x water head above base underside x plan area. Base self weight only=25 x area x thickness; not full building flotation resistance.
